subject: Post-demo recap: hosting preference & audit asks for CareBridge
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khanna <samir@carebridge.io>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@carebridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: hosting preference & audit asks for CareBridge

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of next steps so we can validate the right hosting path for CareBridge (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem).

Key constraints you flagged on the call:
- PHI in inference payloads: full names + SSN-like identifiers in a small subset of records.
- Corporate policy requires a BAA and evidence of controls for data at rest and in transit.
- Possibility of an upcoming external audit in Q3; auditor will want system architecture diagrams and SOC 2 scope.

Preliminary recommendation (based on call):
- Short term: Hosted API with dedicated tenancy controls is feasible if we sign a BAA and apply a per-tenant encryption profile + short retention.
- Mid term (preferred if you want complete network isolation and longer-term audit scoping control): Dedicated capacity or Private VPC. Private VPC gives the cleanest audit path (control plane separation, customer-managed keys).

As discussed, next concrete asks from Redwood so we can finalize the path: 
1) Please confirm whether CareBridge requires customer-managed KMS (HSM) for encryption at rest.
2) Confirm expected retention window for logs and inference inputs (default Redwood retention is 30 days).
3) Identify the likely auditor firm and the expected audit date range (so we can prioritize SOC2 evidence pull).
4) If Private VPC is preferred, confirm whether you need VPC peering or a dedicated on-prem gateway.

Attachments: I attached a short SOC 2 scope overview and our standard BAA template for your legal team to review.

I'll loop Marissa in for evidence scoping and Karthik for infra sizing. Proposed internal owners: Karthik -> infra/ops fit; Marissa -> security evidence/controls.

Proposed timeline: once we have answers to questions 1–4 above, we can produce a comparison (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and a gap list for audit evidence within 3 business days.

Thanks —
Lauren
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

---
Attachments (stubs): redwood_soc2_scope_overview_2026.pdf (PDF, 2.1 MB), redwood_baa_template.docx (DOCX, 42 KB)

From: Samir Khanna <samir@carebridge.io>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@carebridge.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: hosting preference & audit asks for CareBridge

Thanks Lauren — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Customer-managed KMS: Yes, if we go beyond POC we will need CMK in our cloud account (AWS KMS). For POC we can use Redwood-managed keys but must have the option to flip to CMK before production.
2) Retention: We need a hard cutoff of 90 days for inference inputs and logs; PHI payloads should be configurable for automatic purging after 30 days for certain endpoints.
3) Auditor: Likely Crowe (tentative). Audit window is presently mid-September to early October, but we'll confirm exact dates.
4) Private VPC: If we choose this path, we prefer VPC peering (not on-prem gateway) to avoid additional hardware.

Two additional asks: 
- Can you confirm whether Redwood's Hosted API encrypts KV cache at rest by default?
- What evidence do you provide for encryption key rotation and access logs (KMS audit trails)?

We will share a short security questionnaire from our InfoSec team (expected later today). Priya from procurement will start reviewing the BAA.

—Samir
Director of Engineering, CareBridge
samir@carebridge.io

On Thu, May 13, 2027 at 07:08 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khanna <samir@carebridge.io>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@carebridge.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: hosting preference & audit asks for CareBridge

Hi Samir / Priya — looping in from security. Quick notes and what we can produce for the mid-September audit: 

What Redwood can provide today (evidence examples):
- SOC 2 Type II summary report (high-level) and the list of controls in scope — attached in Lauren's email is the scope overview.
- KMS rotation policy + exportable key rotation logs (AWS KMS CloudTrail events) 
- Access logs and audit trails for our control plane (we can provide filtered traces for service accounts and token issuance).
- Network diagrams and segmentation docs (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Specific answers to Samir's questions: 
- KV cache: in Hosted API the KV cache is encrypted at rest with Redwood-managed keys by default. For Dedicated/Private we support CMK (customer-managed keys).
- Key rotation evidence: we can provide KMS audit events and our key-rotation cadence policy. For CMK we can show CloudTrail entries from your account if you choose VPC peering + CMK.

Pending asks (what I'd like from CareBridge):
- The InfoSec questionnaire you mentioned (we'll map responses to evidence).
- Confirm whether the auditor requires encrypted backups or if logical backups (with CMK) are acceptable.

Next steps I propose: 
1) CareBridge shares questionnaire + confirms auditor/date range.
2) Redwood creates a one-page matrix that maps your asks to deliverables for each hosting option (Hosted w/BAA, Dedicated, Private VPC).
3) If you choose Private VPC, we'll schedule an infra scoping call (Karthik to lead).

Happy to jump on a quick 30-min call this week to walk through the matrix.

—Marissa
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: hosting preference & audit asks for CareBridge

Morning — quick infra follow-up and proposed immediate actions so we don't block your PoC timeline: 

Immediate (48–72hr) items we can do: 
- Provide a short matrix (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) that lists: network isolation, key management options, typical SLA/latency delta, and evidence we can provide for audit.
- Share a sample VPC peering checklist and estimated IP ranges for Private VPC (so your infra team can pre-approve firewall rules).
- Confirm that for POC you can use Hosted + Redwood-managed KMS and then flip to CMK prior to production — we will document the flip procedure in runbook form.

For planning: if you prefer Private VPC, expect a 4–6 week timeline for peering, verification, and runbook handoff (shorter if both cloud accounts are ready and we have automation access). Dedicated capacity can be provisioned in ~2–3 weeks but will require a minimum commit.

I'll attach the VPC peering checklist and a short infra sizing note in the matrix we send. Lauren / Marissa, we'll coordinate any legal/security edits to the BAA before Priya reviews.

Karthik
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
